newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean blue chips end higher, led by electricals.
newsitem.headline: Chilean blue chips end higher, led by electricals.

text.p: Chilean blue chips took their cue from Wall Street and closed modestly higher in slow trading, with bullish news in the electrical sector and technical rebounds after four losing sessions in a row.
The blue-chip IPSA index ended 0.13 percent higher at 130.76 points, reflecting gains among big-volume electrical shares.
The general IGPA index slipped 0.29 percent to 5656.11 points on small volume of 10.3 billion pesos traded.

Chilgener, the day's top stock by volume, rose 2.3 percent to 175.50 pesos on a positive outlook for its purchase of a major stake in Peruvian utility Egenor and expectations of good second-quarter results, brokers said.

Chilgener, Chile's largest fossil fuel power generator, announced last Thursday that it was buying a stake in Egenor, giving Chilgener its first stake in the Peruvian power sector after purchases in Argentina, Brazil and Colombia.
Endesa inched up 0.08 percent to 305.25 pesos after the state environmental board Conama gave the green light for Endesa's controversial Ralco dam project.
The market shrugged off figures showing a steady, 3.8 percent growth rate in the gross domestic product in the first quarter, saying the numbers were already factored into prices.
"It was completely within expectations," said one broker.

The impact of the Central Bank's GDP statistics is always muted because they are prefigured by the IMACEC index of economic activity, released on the 23rd day of each month and which gives an early barometer of GDP performance. The IMACEC growth rate for the first quarter, released on May 23, was 3.9 percent.
The market also paid little heed to comments from Finance Minister Eduardo Aninat, who said Chile could beat its official inflation target of 5.5 percent for the year.
"This sort of news is always encouraging but it's more of a sign for foreign investors than for the local market. Around here, everybody already knows it," said a broker.
Other gainers included Vina Concha y Toro, up 1.9 percent to 270 pesos, and smaller wineries Undurraga and Santa Rita, all on a generally good outlook for Chilean wine sales abroad, brokers said.
Decliners included Banco Edwards, off 1.4 percent to 53.25 pesos, and steelmaker CAP, off 3.6 percent to 1215 pesos.
